footpaths.name: Millpond Walk
footpaths.note: The old millrace fed three farms. Its stones still carry the marks of their households.

footpaths.name: Watcher's Knoll
footpaths.note: The old coast guard kept a lantern on this ridge. Below it, the cart road winds east toward Bellharbor.

footpaths.name: The Bell Barrows
footpaths.note: The hill keeps its bell long after the road forgot the name of the king buried here.

footpaths.name: Coppervein Mine
footpaths.note: A blocked mining entrance. Fresh lamp soot stains the wood under the lintel.

footpaths.name: Sluicekeeper's Walk
footpaths.note: The old flood marks cut into the stone tell a different story to the names in the harbor ledger.

footpaths.name: Webbed Deep
footpaths.note: The pass watch used to patrol this cleft. The lantern hooks are still there.

footpaths.name: Vigil Crypt
footpaths.note: The last knights of Ashcourt asked to be buried with their watch bells.

footpaths.name: Rimewatch Reliquary
footpaths.note: Wax drips down the frozen threshold. Someone still tends a light in the snow.

footpaths.name: Siltjack Camp
footpaths.note: The Siltjacks used to guide caravans through the wash. These days they still know exactly where to meet them.

footpaths.name: Sluicekeeper's Pond
footpaths.note: Water from the old sluice backs up into a quiet pool beside the village.

footpaths.name: Heron Oxbow
footpaths.note: The sluice runs past an old reed bed. Fish shelter here when the current is strong.

footpaths.name: Bracken Falls
footpaths.note: A cold spring breaks out of the ridge and feeds the Reedmire sluice all the way to the sea.

footpaths.name: Cutlass Cove
footpaths.note: The Saltglass crews trade under white sails. Red canvas marks the harbor where they unload the rest.

footpaths.name: Smuggler's Cut
footpaths.note: A dune track returns to Saltglass above the cove. The old signal post still faces the anchorage.

footpaths.name: Signalman's Shelf
footpaths.note: The lower road and its three watch lights are visible from the old signal perch.

footpaths.name: Shepherd's White
footpaths.note: In a good winter the sheep came back on their own. Nobody here remembers a good winter.

footpaths.name: Goat Stair
footpaths.note: The old goat track rises to a saddle where the east wind can cross the mountain.

footpaths.name: The Dry Wells
footpaths.note: Three wells follow the old caravan road. Only the western one ever ran dry before the sea changed course.

footpaths.name: Sailcloth Dunes
footpaths.note: When the wind lifts the sand, old mooring stones appear far inland.

footpaths.name: Veilwood Hollow
footpaths.note: The green lights gather at the stones when the last of the daylight goes.

footpaths.name: Old Quarry Road
footpaths.note: Wardens once rang the quarry bell when a loaded wagon started down. Across the hollow you can still see their stone cutting.

footpaths.name: Stonecutters' Way
footpaths.note: The road builders cut through this saddle by lantern light. Names still show on the timber where their tools rested.

footpaths.name: Whitehorn High Shelf
footpaths.note: Old cairns mark the upper shelf. In clear weather the pass looks like a single thread below.

footpaths.name: Three Cairns of Whitehorn
footpaths.note: Someone keeps leaving a blue ribbon here. The wind has only managed to steal two of them.

footpaths.name: Saltglass Bluff
footpaths.note: The first salt carriers marked shoals from here. When the mist lifts you can see which side of the headland they favoured.

footpaths.name: The Tide Ledger
footpaths.note: Four lines carved into a stone record the highest tides remembered by the old harbour master.
